summary: Godefroy de Blonay was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a diploma from the École Pratique des Hautes Études studying under Sylvain Lévi (~1891–1894). He served as Privatdozent of Indology at the University of Neuchâtel (1911–1929).

Active in religious studies, history, archaeology, and Indology, Phillips earned an M.A. from Mansfield College. He was Professor of Church History at United Theological College, Bangalore (1910), Foreign Secretary for the London Missionary Society (1926–1935), and Professor at Kingsmead College (1926–1944).

Working in philosophy and Indology, Narayanaswamy studied at IIT Madras (B.Tech 1990–1994), IISc (M.Sc (Engg) 1994–1997), Annamalai University (M.A. 2015–2017), and IIT Kharagpur (Ph.D. 2020). He held leadership roles at Synergy Infotech, Sonim Technologies, and Itron.

Tsybikov specialized in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Tomsk State University and Saint Petersburg State University under Aleksey Pozdneev, he taught at Eastern Institute, Far Eastern Federal University (~1902–1917), and Irkutsk State University (1928–1930).

Gopal Lal Meena is an Indologist who taught Shagun Sinha. His attested academic appointments include serving as a Professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University and as a Professor emeritus at the University of Delhi (both attested 2026).
Gopikamohan Bhattacharya was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Erich Frauwallner. He held an academic post at Kurukshetra University (attested 1977).

Kaviraj was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at University Maharani College and Allahabad under Arthur Venis, Madhusudan Ojha, and Shashadhar Tarkachuramani. He served as librarian, Principal, and Head of Yoga-Tantra at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University/Government Sanskrit College, Varanasi.

Indologist Gordon Charles Roadarmel studied at Wooster, Chicago Theological Seminary, University of Allahabad, and UC Berkeley (M.A.s 1957, 1962; Ph.D. 1969). He taught Hindi at the University of Chicago (1963–1965) and served as Assistant Professor at UC Berkeley (~1969–1972).

A scholar of religion and philosophy, Kaufman studied at Bethel, Northwestern, and Yale (B.D. ~1948–1951, Ph.D. ~1951–1955). He held posts at Pomona (~1953–1958), Vanderbilt (~1958–1963), and Harvard, where he was Mallinckrodt Professor of Divinity from 1963.

A linguist and Indologist, Fairbanks earned degrees from the University of Alberta and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (Ph.D. 1948). His posts included Southwestern University, Cornell University (1945–1970), Deccan College, the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and UIUC.

Gordon Hannington Luce was a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and linguistics. He studied at Emmanuel College and the University of Cambridge (~1908–1911) and served as a Professor at the University of Rangoon (~1912–1964).

An Indology and history scholar educated at Trinity College, Cambridge, Johnson held fellowships at Trinity and Selwyn. He served as President of Wolfson College (1993–2010), Deputy Vice-Chancellor of Cambridge (1974–2010), and President of the Royal Asiatic Society (2015–2018).

Matthews was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Merton College (M.A. ~1906–1910) and Mansfield College (B.D. ~1910–1912). He was Professor of English and Vice-Principal at Madras Christian College (~1913–1939) and Lecturer in Tamil at SOAS (1939).

Gore Ouseley worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He was affiliated with the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (~1810–1814) and served as Vice-President of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1823–1844).

Gottfried Bernhardy was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. After studying at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1817–1820), he held a long-standing academic post at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1829–1875).

Groddeck was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the Academic Gymnasium Danzig and the University of Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne (~1782–1786). He later held posts at Vilnius University and the Imperial University of Vilna (~1797–1824).

Gottfried Hartmann Weigle worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Evangelische Seminare Maulbronn und Blaubeuren and the University of Tübingen, where he studied under Heinrich Ewald (~1835–1838), and served as a Basel Mission missionary from 1838.

A scholar of linguistics, Hermann studied at the universities of Leipzig and Jena. At Leipzig, he served as extraordinary professor of philosophy (1798) and Director of the philological seminar (1803–1848), and he founded the Griechische Gesellschaft in 1799.

Gottfried Kinkel was a scholar of history and archaeology who studied at the University of Bonn (~1831–1834). He subsequently held posts at the University of Bonn (~1837–1848) and at ETH Zurich (~1866–1882).
Gottlieb L. Schaenzlin was an Indologist. He served as Principal of the Collins Institute in 1914 and later completed an M.A. at Johns Hopkins University (~1920–1921).
